jobs.description:
From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven.

About Us

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on.

Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions.

As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact.

​

During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites.

About the Role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the Semantic Layer team in Bengaluru. You'll own the health, delivery, and growth of the team behind MetricFlow — building and coaching a group of engineers, setting technical direction in partnership with your leads, and ensuring one of the most important projects in the modern data stack keeps shipping with quality and momentum.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll spend most of your time growing people, running a healthy delivery process, and shaping strategy — but you'll stay close enough to the code and the architecture to make sound technical calls and earn the trust of a senior engineering team. You'll also be the steward of a public, community-facing open-source project, balancing the needs of internal roadmap and external contributors.

About the team

The Semantic Layer team owns the systems that turn dbt models into trusted, reusable business metrics. At the heart of this is MetricFlow — the open-source semantic engine that powers the dbt Semantic Layer. MetricFlow lets data teams define metrics once in code and consume them consistently across BI tools, notebooks, AI agents, and downstream applications.

This team is the steward of MetricFlow as an open-source project: shipping releases, reviewing community contributions, evolving the query compiler, and ensuring it integrates cleanly with the broader dbt ecosystem. The team works at the intersection of language design, query compilation, and distributed data execution — solving problems that directly shape how thousands of organizations measure their business.

What you'll do

  • Lead, coach, and grow a team of software engineers building MetricFlow — hiring, onboarding, career development, performance management, and day-to-day support.

  • Own delivery for the Semantic Layer team: planning, prioritization, execution, and predictable shipping of high-quality software.

  • Partner with your senior and staff engineers to set technical direction across metric definitions, query compilation, dimensional modeling, and SQL generation for multiple data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Redshift, and others).

  • Steward MetricFlow as an open-source project — set the bar for how the team triages issues, reviews external pull requests, manages releases, and engages the community on GitHub and in Slack.

  • Collaborate with engineering leaders across the dbt platform, dbt Core, and the Semantic Layer service to ensure MetricFlow integrates seamlessly with the rest of the dbt ecosystem.

  • Partner with product, design, and developer-relations counterparts to translate customer and community feedback into a clear, well-sequenced roadmap.

  • Drive engineering excellence in performance, reliability, and observability of metric query execution at scale.

  • Foster a culture of design docs, thoughtful code review, and durable engineering — shipping fast without shipping sloppy.

Skills we're looking for

  • Experience managing software engineering teams, including hiring, coaching, and performance management, with a track record of shipping production systems.

  • A strong engineering foundation — you've built and shipped production software yourself and can engage credibly on architecture and technical tradeoffs with a senior team.

  • Familiarity with the technical domain: SQL fundamentals, how analytical query engines and data warehouses execute queries, and systems that involve parsing, compilation, or transformation (query planners, DSL compilers, type systems, or rule-based engines).

  • Solid grasp of software design principles: clean APIs, modularity, testability, and backwards compatibility — and the judgment to hold a team to them.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication — you can explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineers, product managers, and external community members.

  • Experience leading in a distributed, asynchronous team environment.

Nice to have

  • Experience leading or contributing to a popular open-source project, including managing a community of external contributors.

  • Familiarity with dbt, MetricFlow, LookML, Cube, or other semantic-layer technologies.

  • Background in data warehousing internals, query optimization, or analytical SQL dialects.

  • Experience with CI/CD, GitHub Actions, and release engineering for Python libraries.

  • Exposure to building developer-facing APIs, SDKs, or CLIs.

Why join us

  • Impact at scale: Your team's code will run inside the data platforms of tens of thousands of companies, including some of the world's largest enterprises.

  • Open-source ownership: You'll lead the team behind a foundational open-source project — visible, reviewed, and used by the global data community.

  • A team that values craft: We invest in design docs, code review, and durable engineering. We ship fast, but we don't ship sloppy.

  • Competitive compensation: Market-leading salary, equity, comprehensive health insurance, generous time off, learning and wellness stipends, and home-office support.

Perks and Benefits

  • 100% employer-paid medical insurance*
  • Generous paid time-off policy (PTO), plus paid sick time, inclusive parental leave policy, holidays (including a year end Global Week of Rest), and volunteer days off
  • RSU stock grants*
  • Professional development and training opportunities
  • Company virtual happy hours, free food, and fun team-building activities
  • Monthly cell phone stipend
  • Access to an innovative mental health support platform that offers personalized care and resources in areas such as: therapy, coaching, and self-guided mindfulness exercises for all covered employees and their covered dependents.

JOB POSTING

SENIOR MANAGER, IMPACT

ABOUT THE CANADIAN PARALYMPIC COMMITTEE

The Canadian Paralympic Committee is a non-profit, private organization in collaboration with 28-member sport organizations. We are deeply committed to harnessing the transformative power and impact of Paralympic sport.

With a vision of fostering an inclusive world through Paralympic sport, our mission emphasizes both the excellence in games preparation and the promotion of inclusive communities. By celebrating the stories and successes of high-performance athletes with disabilities, the Canadian Paralympic Committee aims to inspire all Canadians to embrace inclusivity and actively engage in sports.

Job summary

The Senior Manager, Impact will collaborate closely with the Chief Commercial & Impact Officer to develop and integrate CPC’s organization-wide impact practice, strengthening how initiatives are designed, delivered, measured and communicated, and how investment is translated into meaningful, measurable outcomes.

Supporting both the Canadian Paralympic Committee (CPC) and the Paralympic Foundation of Canada (PFC), the Senior Manager will serve as a key organizational connector. They will bring expertise in impact strategy, program design, measurement and storytelling to help teams strengthen existing initiatives, develop new opportunities and demonstrate the value created for athletes, people with disabilities, communities, partners and the sport system.

This is a strategic and hands-on role. The Senior Manager will lead CPC’s social value and impact measurement practice, strengthen a portfolio of priority initiatives, and help shape opportunities for corporate, philanthropic and government investment. They will also directly lead selected cross-functional initiatives and programs requiring dedicated ownership. Sitting within the Marketing & Communications team, the role will connect evidence with compelling stories and strengthen how CPC communicates its impact and influence.

Type: Full-time

Salary: $78,000- $90,000 annually plus benefits

Reports: Chief Commercial & Impact Officer

Location: Remote within Canada, with travel to CPC head office in Ottawa for occasional in-person meetings.

Main duties and responsibilities

Organization-wide impact leadership

  • Work alongside the CCIO to develop and integrate CPC’s organization-wide impact practice, establishing shared frameworks, capabilities and ways of working.
  • Maintain an organization-wide view of CPC’s impact portfolio and provide recommendations on priorities, sequencing, investment potential, risks, and capacity.
  • Work with program owners to strengthen intended outcomes, delivery models, measurements, and long-term sustainability. Help teams resolve barriers, connect related work, and integrate appropriate lived-experience advisory.
  • Directly lead selected cross-functional impact initiatives and partnerships requiring dedicated ownership.

Impact measurement, social value and learning

  • Lead the development and implementation of CPC’s impact measurement and social value practice. Align CPC’s approach with relevant national and international frameworks, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
  • Develop theories of change, outcomes, indicators, and practical evaluation plans for priority initiatives.
  • Establish proportionate processes for collecting, analyzing and reporting impact evidence with program owners, Finance and external partners.
  • Use evidence and learning to strengthen program design, inform investment decisions, and demonstrate individual, community and system-level change.

Impact reporting and knowledge mobilization

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of impact evidence and stories across CPC and PFC, covering programs, grants, athlete and participant experiences, partner contributions and broader system progress.
  • Work with Marketing & Communications to translate evidence into accessible and respectful stories, and support the development of CPC’s annual Impact Report, case studies, impact summaries and decision materials for partners, funders, government, the Board and members.
  • Translate research, evaluation findings and implementation learning into practical tools and recommendations for CPC and the broader sport system

Cross-functional leadership

  • Build trusted relationships across CPC and with external partners, creating clarity around responsibilities, decisions, timelines, and shared outcomes.
  • Lead planning, budgeting, forecasting, and reporting for assigned initiatives.
  • Manage consultants, researchers, and evaluation partners as required.

OFFRE D’EMPLOI

GESTIONNAIRE PRINCIPAL(E), IMPACT

À PROPOS DU COMITÉ PARALYMPIQUE CANADIEN

Le Comité paralympique canadien est un organisme privé sans but lucratif qui collabore avec 28 organismes de sport membres. Il est résolument déterminé à exploiter le pouvoir de transformation et la portée du sport paralympique.

Sa vision est de promouvoir le sport paralympique comme tremplin vers un monde inclusif. Sa mission met l’accent sur l’excellence lors de la préparation pour les Jeux, ainsi que sur la promotion de collectivités inclusives. En célébrant les parcours et les réussites des athlètes de haut niveau ayant un handicap, le Comité paralympique canadien souhaite inciter les Canadiennes et les Canadiens à adopter l’inclusion et à s’engager activement dans le sport.

Résumé des fonctions

La personne titulaire du poste de gestionnaire principal(e), Impact, travaillera en étroite collaboration avec le chef/la cheffe de la direction commerciale et de l’impact (CDCI), afin d’élaborer et d’intégrer une approche organisationnelle en matière d’impact au sein du Comité paralympique canadien (CPC). Elle contribuera ainsi à renforcer la conception, la mise en œuvre, l’évaluation et la communication des initiatives de l’organisation, ainsi qu’à transformer les investissements en résultats concrets, significatifs et mesurables.

Au service du CPC et de la Fondation paralympique canadienne (la Fondation), elle jouera un rôle clé de liaison au sein de l’organisation. Elle mettra à profit son expertise en stratégie d’impact, en conception de programmes, en mesure des résultats et en communication narrative afin d’aider les équipes à renforcer les initiatives existantes, à élaborer de nouvelles possibilités et à mettre en évidence la valeur créée pour les athlètes, les personnes en situation de handicap, les communautés, les partenaires et le système sportif.

Il s’agit d’un poste à la fois stratégique et concret. La personne titulaire dirigera les activités du CPC liées à la valeur sociale et à la mesure de l’impact, renforcera un portefeuille d’initiatives prioritaires et contribuera à définir des possibilités d’investissement pour les entreprises, les donatrices et donateurs, ainsi que les administrations publiques. Elle pilotera également certaines initiatives et certains programmes interfonctionnels nécessitant une responsabilité clairement attribuée. Relevant de l’équipe du marketing et des communications, la personne titulaire du poste fera le lien entre les données probantes et des récits convaincants, et renforcera ce faisant la façon dont le CPC communique son impact et son influence.

Type : Temps plein

Salaire : Salaire annuel de 78 000 à 90 000 $, plus avantages sociaux

Relève : Du chef/de la cheffe de la direction commerciale et de l’impact

Lieu : À distance, au Canada, avec des déplacements occasionnels au siège social du CPC, à Ottawa, pour des réunions en présentiel

Tâches et responsabilités principales

Leadership en matière d’impact à l’échelle de l’organisation

  • Collaborer avec le/la CDCI à l’élaboration et à l’intégration de la pratique du CPC en matière d’impact à l’échelle de l’organisation, notamment par la mise en place de cadres, de capacités et de méthodes de travail communs.
  • Maintenir une vue d’ensemble du portefeuille d’initiatives d’impact du CPC et formuler des recommandations quant aux priorités, à l’ordre de mise en œuvre, au potentiel d’investissement, aux risques et à la capacité organisationnelle.
  • Collaborer avec les responsables de programmes au renforcement des résultats visés, des modèles de prestation, des mesures et de la viabilité à long terme. Aider les équipes à surmonter les obstacles, à créer des liens entre les travaux connexes et à intégrer, lorsque cela est pertinent, les conseils de personnes ayant une expérience vécue.
  • Piloter directement certaines initiatives et certains partenariats interfonctionnels en matière d’impact nécessitant une prise en charge attitrée.

Mesure de l’impact, valeur sociale et apprentissage

  • Diriger l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de la pratique du CPC en matière de mesure de l’impact et de valeur sociale. Harmoniser l’approche du CPC avec les cadres nationaux et internationaux pertinents, notamment les objectifs de développement durable des Nations Unies.
  • Élaborer des théories du changement, des résultats, des indicateurs et des plans d’évaluation concrets pour les initiatives prioritaires.
  • Établir, en collaboration avec les responsables de programmes, l’équipe des finances et les partenaires externes, des processus adaptés à l’envergure des initiatives pour recueillir, analyser et communiquer les données probantes sur l’impact.
  • Mettre à profit les données probantes et les apprentissages pour améliorer la conception des programmes, éclairer les décisions d’investissement et démontrer les changements à l’échelle des personnes, des collectivités et des systèmes.

Rapports sur l’impact et mobilisation des connaissances

  • Constituer et alimenter un flux continu de données probantes et de récits sur l’impact au sein du CPC et de la Fondation, portant notamment sur les programmes, les subventions, l’expérience des athlètes et des personnes participantes, les contributions des partenaires et les progrès réalisés à l’échelle du système.
  • Collaborer avec l’équipe du marketing et des communications afin de présenter les données probantes sous forme de récits accessibles et respectueux, et contribuer à la production du rapport annuel sur l’impact du CPC, d’études de cas, de synthèses sur l’impact et de documents d’aide à la décision destinés aux partenaires, aux bailleurs de fonds, aux gouvernements, au conseil d’administration et aux membres.
  • Transformer les résultats de recherche, les constats d’évaluation et les apprentissages tirés de la mise en œuvre en outils pratiques et en recommandations à l’intention du CPC et de l’ensemble du système sportif.

Leadership interfonctionnel

  • Établir des relations de confiance au sein du CPC et avec les partenaires externes, en veillant à clarifier les responsabilités, les décisions, les échéanciers et les résultats communs.
  • Diriger la planification, la budgétisation, les prévisions et la production de rapports pour les initiatives qui lui sont confiées.
  • Gérer les consultantes et consultants, les chercheuses et chercheurs, ainsi que les partenaires d’évaluation, au besoin.
  • Représenter le CPC au sein de certains groupes de travail, dans le cadre de consultations et lors d’initiatives sectorielles.
  • Pendant les Jeux et d’autres événements d’envergure, assumer un rôle interfonctionnel déterminé en fonction des priorités organisationnelles. Ce rôle peut notamment consister à mettre en œuvre des initiatives stratégiques, à soutenir les parties prenantes et les programmes communautaires, ou à contribuer aux relations avec les partenaires et les gouvernements.

Qualifications

  • Au moins sept ans d’expérience dans des fonctions aux responsabilités croissantes dans les domaines de l’impact social, de la mise en œuvre de stratégies, de l’élaboration de programmes, de l’évaluation, des partenariats ou dans un domaine connexe.
  • Expérience démontrée dans le renforcement d’initiatives complexes et dans la réalisation de projets interfonctionnels, de leur conception à leur mise en œuvre.
  • Expérience dans l’élaboration de théories du changement, de cadres de résultats, d’indicateurs et de méthodes d’évaluation concrètes.
  • Expérience dans la présentation de données probantes et de résultats de programmes sous forme de rapports clairs, d’argumentaires d’investissement et de récits convaincants.
  • Solides aptitudes pour la réflexion stratégique, la direction de projets, la rédaction analytique, les présentations et l’établissement de relations.
  • Expérience dans l’exercice d’une influence auprès de différentes équipes et dans la collaboration avec l’équipe dirigeante, des bailleurs de fonds, des partenaires commerciaux, des organismes communautaires et d’autres groupes complexes de parties prenantes.
  • Formation postsecondaire pertinente et/ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.

Les qualifications suivantes sont considérées comme des atouts :

  • Expérience dans l’élaboration de partenariats ou de propositions axés sur l’impact afin d’obtenir des investissements d’entreprises, d’organisations philanthropiques ou d’administrations publiques.
  • Connaissance des enjeux liés à l’accessibilité et à l’inclusion des personnes en situation de handicap, du modèle social du handicap, des objectifs de développement durable des Nations Unies ou des méthodes de mesure de la valeur sociale.
  • Expérience professionnelle dans le milieu sportif et auprès d’athlètes, de personnes en situation de handicap ou de conseillères et conseillers ayant une expérience vécue.
  • Bilinguisme (anglais-français)

Profil individuel

  • Esprit stratégique, sens pratique et souci d’obtenir des résultats.
  • Aptitude à passer des priorités organisationnelles aux détails de la mise en œuvre.
  • Esprit d’initiative, débrouillardise et capacité à faire avancer les projets dans un environnement complexe.
  • Esprit analytique et aisance à travailler avec des données probantes, des considérations financières et des récits humains.
  • Esprit de collaboration, crédibilité et capacité à exercer une influence auprès de différentes équipes.
  • Engagement envers l’accessibilité, l’inclusion, l’impact social et le mouvement paralympique.

CONDITIONS DE TRAVAIL

  • Environnement de travail à distance : le candidat retenu/la candidate retenue travaillera principalement depuis le Canada et se rendra au bureau si nécessaire.

  • Le personnel basé à l’extérieur d’Ottawa devra se rendre à Ottawa plusieurs fois par an ou selon les besoins liés au poste.
  • Des déplacements de plus de 24 heures et à l’étranger, ainsi que du travail hors site, seront nécessaires pour les Jeux, les visites de sites, les événements et les réunions
  • Il sera nécessaire de travailler les soirs et les fins de semaine lors des périodes chargées, notamment pendant les Jeux et lors d’autres événements spéciaux.

jobs.excerpt: Junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor (Consultant) We are looking for a junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor to join Harper James on a flexible, freelance consultancy basis.
jobs.description:
Junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor (Consultant)

We are looking for a junior Commercial Litigation Barrister or Solicitor to join Harper James on a flexible, freelance consultancy basis.

This is an excellent opportunity to support a growing and diverse client base, ranging from innovative start-ups and scale-ups to established national and international businesses. You will assist our litigation team with the preparation and progression of court proceedings within a modern, tech-enabled law firm.

Working as part of our flexible consultant model, you will have the autonomy to manage agreed workstreams while benefiting from the support, infrastructure and collaborative culture of a forward-thinking national firm.

What you’ll be doing

You will support senior members of the Commercial Litigation team with the preparation, management and conduct of court litigation.

The role will suit an organised and detail-focused lawyer who is confident handling procedural work, drafting, evidence preparation and case administration to a high standard.

Your work is likely to include:

  • Assisting with the preparation and drafting of statements of case, applications, witness statements, chronologies and other court documents

  • Conducting legal and factual research to support live disputes and litigation strategy

  • Reviewing, organising and analysing documentary evidence

  • Preparing trial bundles, hearing bundles and electronic bundles in accordance with court requirements

  • Assisting with disclosure exercises, including document review, categorisation and preparation of disclosure lists

  • Drafting correspondence with clients, opponents, counsel, courts and other relevant parties

  • Preparing case summaries, attendance notes, hearing notes and internal updates

  • Supporting the preparation of applications, hearings, mediations and trials

  • Assisting with the management of court deadlines, procedural timetables and case management requirements

  • Liaising with clients to obtain instructions, documents and witness evidence

  • Supporting senior solicitors and barristers with the efficient day-to-day management of litigation matters

You may also have the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across the wider Harper James legal team where disputes intersect with corporate, commercial, employment, intellectual property, real estate or insolvency matters.

What we’re looking for

A UK qualified Barrister or Solicitor with experience in commercial litigation and court procedure.

  • Junior-level experience, with the confidence to assist on active litigation matters under appropriate supervision

  • Strong knowledge of the Civil Procedure Rules and practical experience of litigation processes

  • Experience preparing court documents, bundles, chronologies and evidence

  • Excellent legal research, drafting and analytical skills

  • Strong attention to detail, particularly in relation to procedural requirements and document management

  • Ability to work efficiently, independently and flexibly while managing competing priorities

  • Clear and professional communication skills, both written and verbal

  • A pragmatic, client-focused approach and an interest in supporting ambitious businesses through dispute resolution

  • Experience working with electronic disclosure, e-bundling or litigation technology would be advantageous

The Harper James difference

We are a tech-driven, agile law firm where lawyers are empowered with modern legal technology to maximise efficiency, productivity and work-life balance. Our consultant model offers flexibility, autonomy and the ability to work remotely, while remaining part of a supportive national team.

At Harper James, we keep things straightforward. We are relaxed and informal but well organised.

There are no politics and no big egos, if people around us succeed, so do we. We welcome proactive, self-motivated lawyers who thrive in a modern legal environment and are passionate about delivering exceptional client service.

The bottom line

This is an opportunity to play an important role in supporting the continued growth of our Commercial Litigation team, working alongside experienced colleagues and a great team of people who all contribute to our shared success.

Flexible working within a fully remote but collaborative team. Ad hoc attendance at our office in the centre of Birmingham is likely from time-to-time depending on work requirements.

We are offering a competitive consultancy rate, with flexibility and autonomy as part of the Harper James consultant model.

NO AGENCIES PLEASE

Nurse Practitioner – Virtual Care

Work from home as a Nurse Practitioner with flexible scheduling models available

Fonemed is expanding its services and is looking for passionate and dedicated Nurse Practitioners to add to its exceptional and growing team in a work from home telehealth position. At Fonemed, you will have the opportunity to work with a team of over 50 Nurse Practitioners and to create a schedule that works for you. You will assess patients using telephone and video technology. Through virtual care, we meet and provide care for individuals where they are. If you share the company’s passion to defy the conventional boundaries of time and distance to get the right care to the right patient when and where it is needed the most, apply today!

Position Overview

The Nurse Practitioner is responsible to provide appropriate assessment and care to patients in a virtual clinic environment. The successful applicant works independently in diagnosing conditions, prescribing medications, performing, or ordering diagnostic tests and treatments, evaluating treatments, and providing follow-up care within the continuum of care. The Nurse Practitioner provides comprehensive and holistic nursing care to clients including health promotion, injury and illness treatment and prevention.

As an advanced practitioner, the Nurse Practitioner functions in the roles of practitioner, educator, and leader. As governed by provincial regulations, he/she practices independently, collaborating with other healthcare professionals including primary care physicians for issues outside the Nurse Practitioner scope of practice.

Essential Duties:

  • Assessing client presentation, evaluating urgency of care needed, selecting appropriate level of care, facilitating referrals to other providers where appropriate, and determining follow up required
  • Independently and collaboratively assesses, diagnoses, and prescribes in accordance with professional standards, legislation, policies, and clinical practice guidelines
  • Coordinates treatment plans and follow up based on appropriate assessments, client and family response and outcomes, collaborating with other healthcare professionals if needed
  • Communicates findings and diagnosis to client and/or inter-professional team. Discusses prognosis, treatment options and outcomes with client and/or other team members within the circle of care and documents within the client's permanent health record
  • Advocates for clients, assessing their needs and if applicable, referring to appropriate care providers, professionals, or other services in the interest of the continuum of care
  • Follow best practice guidelines

Qualifications:
  • Graduation from a Nurse Practitioner program
  • Current or willingness to obtain licensure as a Nurse Practitioner with the College of Registered Nurses of Newfoundland and Labrador
  • Graduation from an approved School of Nursing
  • Preferred 1 year of recent experience as a practicing Nurse Practitioner preferred. Previous clinical experience will be considered
  • Experience working in emergency or urgent care considered an asset
  • Demonstrated knowledge of home and community health services
  • Family All Ages (FAA) is required
  • Experience practicing in a rural setting considered an asset
  • Exceptional clinical assessment and decision-making abilities
  • Demonstrated leadership qualities and problem-solving skills
  • Strong oral and written communication skills
  • Demonstrated ability to work well independently and in a collaborative team environment
  • Must have very strong computer and technology skills to be able to deliver virtual care through the use of technology
  • Experience and aptitude with e-consult is an asset
  • A commitment to professional development
  • A passion for telehealth and an advocate for the benefits and opportunities that telehealth offers to patients and clients
  • A satisfactory background screening result
  • You must have your own computer system with 2 monitors, USB headset, webcam, and high-speed internet connection to connect through VPN

We are flexible in offering either full time or part time and offer a competitive compensation package.

Why Work With Us

With over 20 years in the telehealth industry servicing clients across North America, Fonemed prides itself on providing outstanding client experience and practicing a culture of care in everything we do. We are a growing company who values our greatest resource - our people! We provide a collaborative company culture and a welcoming team. We offer our team the opportunity to work in an exciting industry and a competitive compensation package, including health benefits and retirement saving options, as well as a great paid leave program. If you are looking for an opportunity to work from home for a company that values you, apply today!

Fonemed is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to diversity. We appreciate the interest of everyone who applies for the position, however only those selected for an interview will be contacted. Please visit our website at www.fonemed.com.

jobs.excerpt: Built's Mission: Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.
jobs.description:
Built's Mission: Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at getbuilt.com.

Product Designer II

About The Role

Built Technologies is the AI-first platform for construction and real estate finance, trusted by Goldman Sachs, Fifth Third, and 45 of the top 100 U.S. banks to manage over $300 billion in annual capital. The design challenges at Built are genuinely complex: the lenders, owners, developers, and contractors using our platform are navigating high-stakes financial workflows where clarity, accuracy, and trust are not nice-to-haves — they are requirements. Making those workflows feel simple and human without sacrificing depth is the central design problem. The Product Designer II is a practitioner ready to own meaningful pieces of that problem independently.

This role is for a designer who has built a solid foundation and is ready to drive design decisions with greater autonomy. You independently own design work across features and product areas with growing complexity, lead research activities, and are actively developing your ability to scope problems and communicate design rationale to cross-functional partners.

Our Guiding Principles

  • Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don’t hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.
  • Help Customers Win. We learn our customers’ businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.
  • Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.
  • Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don’t wait to be asked.
  • Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

What You’ll Do

  • Own design execution for features and workflows across Built’s platform — from discovery through delivery — including the draw management, budget tracking, and compliance surfaces that lenders and borrowers depend on.
  • Lead user research activities including customer interviews, usability tests, and synthesis sessions — becoming a genuine expert in how lenders, owners, contractors, and inspectors use Built.
  • Create user flows, journey maps, wireframes, and high-fidelity mockups with increasing complexity — choosing the right fidelity for the question at hand rather than defaulting to one approach.
  • Collaborate closely with product managers and engineers to ensure designs are feasible, well-understood, and implemented with fidelity to intent.
  • Contribute to and maintain the design system, identifying opportunities to improve shared components and patterns across the product portfolio.
  • Clearly articulate design decisions and trade-offs to cross-functional stakeholders — framing rationale in terms of user needs and business outcomes, not just aesthetics. • Incorporate data and behavioral insights to validate and iterate on design solutions — using evidence to challenge your own assumptions.
  • Support more junior designers through informal feedback and collaboration, sharing your process and approach openly.

What You’ll Bring

  • 2–4+ years of experience in product or UX design within a SaaS or digital product environment.
  • Strong proficiency in Figma and prototyping tools — you work efficiently at multiple fidelity levels and prototype thoughtfully to answer specific questions.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle end-to-end design for product features independently — from research and problem framing through execution and QA.
  • Solid understanding of UX research methods and when to apply them — you know the difference between generative and evaluative research and can lead both. • A portfolio showing thoughtful problem-framing and well-executed design solutions — work that reflects how you think, not just the final output.
  • A clear and confident communicator who can present work, defend decisions, and incorporate feedback without becoming defensive.
  • Attention to accessibility and inclusive design best practices is a meaningful plus.

What Success Looks Like at Six Months

  • You are independently owning design for at least one feature area — from research through shipped experience — and the quality of what ships reflects your design intent. • Product managers and engineers treat you as a reliable, proactive design partner who contributes perspective beyond just executing to spec.
  • You have led at least one user research session with real customers and used the findings to inform or adjust a design direction.
  • Your design system contributions are accurate, well-considered, and improve consistency across the product.
  • You are developing genuine depth in construction finance domain knowledge — you understand Built’s customer segments and can explain how design decisions affect their real work.

AI & Technology Expectations

  • Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work.
  • Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role.
  • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.
  • Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights. • Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

Built’s salary range for this position is $100,000 - 125,000 USD per year. The pay range is designed to accommodate upward mobility in the role, therefore it encompasses the full span of proficiency levels for this role and we believe that the midpoint of the range is competitive in the market. Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.

Travel Requirement: Employees who are not based in the Nashville area are required to travel to our Nashville office at least twice per year for company gatherings, such as Connect Week. Additional travel to Nashville may be required based on your role and business needs.

Perks:

  • The rare opportunity to radically disrupt a $1.5T industry
  • Competitive benefits including: uncapped vacation [US ONLY], medical, dental & vision insurance
  • Robust compensation package, including equity in the form of stock options

jobs.excerpt: About Us and Why We’re Hiring Terra Energy is a fast-growing residential solar installation company operating across Florida and Texas.
jobs.description:
About Us and Why We’re Hiring

Terra Energy is a fast-growing residential solar installation company operating across Florida and Texas. As we scale our operations, we are building an in-house engineering team to support plan review, inspection services, and installation quality assurance — allowing us to move faster, maintain higher standards, and deliver exceptional outcomes for our customers and installation crews.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced Florida-licensed Plans Examiner (PX) with strong knowledge of residential construction, permitting, and code compliance to join our team.

This position will primarily focus on reviewing residential solar permit packages submitted throughout Florida, ensuring compliance with the Florida Building Code, National Electrical Code, local amendments, and applicable jurisdictional requirements.

The ideal candidate will have experience working with Florida municipalities, private provider services, residential construction, and solar permitting processes.

What You’ll Be Doing

Private Provider Plan Review (PPR)

Review residential solar permit packages on behalf of Authorities Having Jurisdiction (AHJs) and private provider programs to ensure compliance with applicable building, structural, and electrical codes prior to permit issuance.

Plan Review

  • Review residential solar PV permit packages for compliance with Florida Building Code requirements.
  • Examine architectural, structural, electrical, and site plans for code compliance and permit readiness.
  • Verify compliance with NEC, Florida Building Code, ASCE 7 wind loading requirements, and local jurisdictional amendments.
  • Review engineering calculations, attachment details, equipment specifications, and load analyses.
  • Identify deficiencies and provide clear plan review comments for correction and resubmittal.
  • Coordinate with internal design teams, engineers, project managers, and permitting staff to resolve plan review comments efficiently.
  • Maintain familiarity with permitting requirements across Florida municipalities and counties.
  • Support permit approval efforts and reduce turnaround times through efficient plan review processes.

Code Compliance

  • Interpret and apply Florida Building Code provisions and local amendments.
  • Ensure permit packages comply with applicable residential construction standards.
  • Stay current with updates to Florida Building Code, National Electrical Code, and industry best practices.
  • Assist in developing internal code review standards, checklists, and quality control procedures.

Process Improvement

  • Help establish and improve Terra Energy's private provider plan review program.
  • Support standardization of permit package templates and review workflows.
  • Collaborate with engineering, operations, and permitting teams to improve submission quality and approval rates.
  • Provide technical guidance regarding permitting and code compliance issues.

What We’re Looking For

  • Active Florida Plans Examiner (PX) License.
  • Minimum 3 years of experience performing plan reviews, code compliance reviews, permitting, or construction-related inspections.
  • Strong knowledge of Florida Building Code (FBC), National Electrical Code (NEC), and residential construction practices.
  • Experience reviewing construction plans, permit applications, and technical documentation.
  • Familiarity with Florida AHJ permitting processes across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify code compliance issues.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
  • Proficiency with permitting software, digital plan review platforms, and Microsoft Office applications.
  • Familiarity with Florida AHJ permitting processes and inspection requirements across multiple jurisdictions
  • Ability to perform remote video-based and photo-based inspections with clarity and confidence
  • Proficiency with solar design software (Aurora, Helioscope, or equivalent)
  • Strong communication skills — able to effectively coach field installers and interface with AHJ officials

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience reviewing residential solar photovoltaic (PV) systems.
  • Experience working as a Florida Private Provider.
  • Additional Florida certifications such as Building Inspector (BN), Building Official (BO), Electrical Plans Examiner (EP), or Electrical Inspector (EI).
  • Experience working directly with Florida municipalities and county building departments.
  • Knowledge of SolarAPP+ and streamlined permitting programs.
  • Familiarity with utility interconnection requirements.
  • Previous experience supporting high-volume residential permitting operations.

How You’ll Work at Terra Energy

We’re a fast-growing company, and while we move quickly, we rely on strong operational foundations.

You’ll have ownership over your area, direct collaboration with multiple teams, and the opportunity to improve how permitting is handled as we scale.

We value people who are proactive, solution-oriented, and focused on getting things done the right way.

Additional Details

  • Location: Remote (United States)
  • Reports to: Operations Manager
  • Department: Operations

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role means consistently delivering accurate and timely plan reviews that support faster permit approvals while ensuring full compliance with Florida Building Code requirements, NEC standards, and local jurisdictional regulations. The ideal candidate serves as a trusted code compliance expert, identifies and resolves plan deficiencies efficiently, helps reduce permit turnaround times, and collaborates closely with design, engineering, and permitting teams to improve submission quality and approval rates. Their contributions directly support Terra Energy's ability to scale operations, maintain high standards, and accelerate residential solar deployment across Florida.

In Summary

The Florida Licensed Plans Examiner (PX) will join to our growing private provider plan review team. This is a primarily remote position focused on reviewing residential solar permit packages, ensuring code compliance, and supporting faster permit approvals across Florida. The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented code professional who enjoys collaborating with permitting, design, and engineering teams while helping drive the growth of renewable energy.

jobs.excerpt: At DICK’S Sporting Goods, we believe in how positively sports can change lives.
jobs.description:
At DICK’S Sporting Goods, we believe in how positively sports can change lives. On our team, everyone plays a critical role in creating confidence and excitement by personally equipping all athletes to achieve their dreams. We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse workforce, reflecting the communities we serve.

If you are ready to make a difference as part of the world’s greatest sports team, apply to join our team today!

OVERVIEW:

Job Duties & Responsibilities

Strategy and Long-Term Planning

The Director defines and owns the Media Planning team's long-range strategy, ensuring it is aligned with DMN's commercial objectives, annual OKRs, and the broader commerce media landscape. This includes:

  • Building and maintaining the strategic storytelling frameworks that govern how DMN positions its media products to brand partners, including audience narratives, channel value propositions, and performance proof points.

  • Defining the annual priorities and key results for the Media Planning function, cascading them into team-level goals and tracking progress with rigor throughout the year.

  • Establishing DMN's point of view on emerging media planning trends, audience strategies, measurement methodologies, and competitive positioning, and bringing that perspective into plans and client conversations.

  • Communicating the team's strategic direction and performance to internal leadership on a weekly basis, including flagging risks, surfacing opportunities, and advocating for resources and tooling investments.

People Leadership and Team Development

The Director directly manages a media planning manager, with accountability for the performance, development, and culture of the full media planning team. Responsibilities include:

  • Setting clear performance expectations and development plans for each team member, conducting regular 1:1s and formal reviews, and recognizing and rewarding high performance consistently.

  • Recruiting and onboarding top media planning talent, with an emphasis on candidates who combine strong analytical instincts with the ability to build a compelling narrative around data.

  • Identifying skill gaps across the team and designing or sourcing the training, tools, and experiences needed to close them, with a particular focus on retail and commerce media fluency and storytelling craft.

  • Building a team culture that prizes intellectual rigor, creative problem-solving, and collaborative client service, and that attracts strong talent.

  • Build effective teams that apply their diverse skills and perspectives to achieve common goals by establishing common objectives and a shared mindset.

  • Manage execution responsibilities and workload of direct/indirect reports to achieve functional deliverables on time and with quality.

  • Develops talent through coaching, feedback, exposure, and stretch assignments in order to meet their own career goals as well as the organization’s priorities

  • Establish strategic staffing and succession plans; successfully deliver on proposed staffing objectives.

  • Drive the talent selection process in alignment with the company’s talent philosophy for open direct/indirect reporting positions; Ensure all direct reports are appropriately trained and on-boarded.

  • Drive engagement by creating a climate where people are motivated to do their best to help the organization achieve its objectives; focus on voice of teammate data (e.g., Engagement & Pulse results), partnering with organization leadership to drive necessary changes.

Media Strategy and Plan Quality

The Director is ultimately accountable for the quality and strategic coherence of every media plan produced by the team. This means:

  • Establishing and enforcing the standard for what a great plan looks like, including how audience data is surfaced, how channel recommendations are structured and justified, how performance projections are modeled, and how the narrative ties objectives to outcomes.

  • Reviewing and providing substantive feedback on plans before they go to clients, ensuring they meet the strategic bar, are free of errors, and are positioned to generate brand confidence and investment.

  • Building reusable planning templates, data-driven benchmarks, and storytelling frameworks that enable planners to work more efficiently and consistently without sacrificing strategic depth.

  • Staying close to brand and category-level trends to ensure plans are informed by what is actually happening in the market, not just by channel inventory and audience availability.

Tooling, Product, and Process Influence

The Director actively shapes how the Media Planning team works by influencing the tools, systems, and workflows available to them. Responsibilities include:

  • Maintaining a clear point of view on what tools and product features would most meaningfully improve the quality and efficiency of the planning process, and advocating for those investments through structured product partnership engagements.

  • Working with product and engineering teams to scope, prioritize, and test new planning capabilities, audience tools, and data visualization features, representing the planner's perspective in the product roadmap process.

  • Establishing standard operating procedures for plan development, approval workflows, version control, and client handoff that scale as the team and portfolio grow.

  • Identifying and eliminating friction in the planning process.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

The Director represents the Media Planning function across the organization and ensures it is well-connected to the teams it most closely supports and depends on. This includes:

  • Partnering with Sales and Account Management to ensure plans are produced on the timelines clients need, are responsive to the commercial context of each opportunity, and are positioned to close business and retain investment.

  • Collaborating with Analytics and Reporting to ensure that performance measurement methodologies, attribution approaches, and reporting frameworks are reflected accurately in how plans are built and how expectations are set with clients.

  • Engaging with the Monetization team to ensure that new inventory, audience, and targeting capabilities are understood by the planning team and incorporated into plans as soon as they are available.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's Degree

  • 7 - 10 years with 8+ years of experience in media planning, media strategy, or a related discipline, with at least 5 years in a people management role.

  • Demonstrated ability to build data-informed media strategies and translate quantitative analysis into compelling, accessible narratives that drive executive and client alignment.

  • Deep familiarity with the retail and commerce media landscape, including how sponsored products, onsite display, offsite programmatic, CTV, and social channels operate and how brands evaluate their value.

  • Proven track record of developing media plans that win business and deliver measurable performance outcomes against advertiser objectives.

  • Experience influencing cross-functional teams and stakeholders without direct authority, and building productive working relationships across Sales, Account Management, Analytics, and Product.

  • Strong presentation and communication skills, with the ability to distill complex planning rationale into clear, persuasive narratives for senior audiences

  • Analytical proficiency: comfortable working with audience data, reach and frequency models, performance benchmarks, and campaign measurement methodologies.

  • Preferred prior experience at a retail media network, commerce media platform, or major publisher, with direct exposure to first-party audience data activation and closed-loop measurement.

  • Preferred familiarity with media mix modeling (MMM), multi-touch attribution, and incrementality testing, and the ability to apply those frameworks to how plans are structured and sold.

  • Preferred experience working with or alongside media agencies, with an understanding of how brands and agencies evaluate media investment decisions in a retail media context.

  • Preferred background in media planning tools, audience analytics platforms, or data visualization tools, with a track record of advocating for and adopting technology that improves team output.

Transforme o futuro do RD Vendas conosco. Faça parte da evolução da nossa arquitetura e desenvolva soluções escaláveis que geram impacto real para milhares de clientes. jobs.description:
Position Title: Associate Major Gifts Officer
Location: Remote, with travel for cultivation and stewardship events
Reports to: Director of Individual Giving

Hours per week (average): 40

Overtime Status: Exempt

Level: 4

The Role

Manage a portfolio of mid-level donors and emerging major donor prospects, building relationships, increasing engagement, and advancing donors toward deeper investment in the organization. Alongside individual portfolio management, this role owns the one-to-many fundraising program for annual fund donors — a combination of digital outreach, targeted communications, and virtual community moments designed to keep this audience connected and moving toward deeper engagement. This role works closely across the development team on program execution, and requires comfort both designing a cultivation email series and speaking directly with a donor who has just made their first $2,500 gift.

The organization operates across two entities with distinct compliance requirements: Galvanize USA (501(c)(3), tax-deductible contributions and Galvanize Action (501(c)(4), supporting persuasion programming. The Associate MGO must understand the distinctions between these entities and keep all donor communications appropriately scoped.

Core Responsibilities

Portfolio Management, Mid-Level Contributors

  • Manage a portfolio of mid-level donors and emerging major donor prospects, with an emphasis on those who have the capacity to grow their investment over time.
  • Build genuine relationships with portfolio donors through consistent, personalized outreach, including calls, handwritten notes, impact briefings, and invitations to relevant events.
  • Develop and execute tailored cultivation and solicitation plans for each donor in the portfolio, in coordination with the Director of Individual Giving.
  • Use research and evaluation findings — including RCT results, tracking survey data, and program impact updates — as tools for donor conversation and stewardship, connecting each donor to the evidence behind the work their gift supports.
  • Identify donors in the portfolio with the capacity and inclination to move into a major gifts relationship, and work with the Director to structure appropriate upgrade pathways and introductions.
  • Track all activity in EveryAction with rigor and consistency, maintaining accurate contact records, call notes, next steps, and gift dates across the full portfolio.

One-to-Many Fundraising, Annual Fund

  • Own the strategy and execution of the one-to-many fundraising program for annual fund donors, including the content calendar, communication cadence, and revenue targets, in coordination with the Director of Individual Giving.
  • Design and deploy digital outreach — including email appeals, cultivation sequences, and upgrade campaigns — that reflect the voice and values of the organization and keep donors in this range connected to the work.
  • Build and manage a calendar of virtual community moments, including online briefings, research share-outs, and donor conversations, designed to deepen engagement for this segment and move promising donors toward individual cultivation.
  • Ensure program content is accurate, well-timed, and aligned with the broader cultivation strategy across entities.
  • Use data and testing to refine the program over time, tracking open rates, conversion rates, upgrade rates, and retention across the donor segment.

Stewardship and Retention

  • Ensure that every portfolio donor receives timely, meaningful stewardship that connects them to the impact of their gift.
  • Develop differentiated stewardship approaches for donors at different levels, balancing personalization with the scale requirements of a one-to-many program.
  • Write and send personalized acknowledgments, impact updates, and year-end communications for portfolio donors.
  • Keep all stewardship communications appropriately scoped to the entity the donor has given to, with clear, accurate messaging about the purpose of each entity's programming.

Compliance and Entity Clarity

  • Maintain a thorough working knowledge of the distinctions between Galvanize USA (c3) and Galvanize Action (c4)), and apply that knowledge to every donor communication.
  • Flag any compliance questions before sending communications or making solicitations that touch multiple entities.

Team and Systems

  • Maintain strong EveryAction discipline across the full portfolio and one-to-many program, with consistent documentation of every donor touchpoint, gift, and next step.
  • Participate in regular portfolio reviews with the Director of Individual Giving and the broader development team.
  • Contribute to the team's collective knowledge of the donor base, flagging patterns, opportunities, and risks as they emerge.
  • All employees of Hopewell Fund are required to complete timesheets every two weeks.
  • Perform other duties as needed.

Required Qualifications, Education, and Experience

  • Three or more years of fundraising experience, with direct experience managing a donor portfolio and building genuine relationships with mid-level or major donors.
  • Experience with one-to-many fundraising programs, including digital appeals, cultivation sequences, and community-based donor engagement.
  • Experience with EveryAction or a comparable CRM, with a real commitment to documentation discipline.
  • Candidates must be authorized to work in the US. We are not able to sponsor visas at this time.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Strong writing skills, with the ability to produce donor communications that feel personal, specific, and grounded in the organization’s work.
  • A relational orientation, genuine warmth, and the ability to earn trust with donors across a range of giving levels and backgrounds.
  • The ability to manage a portfolio and a program at the same time, with strong organizational instincts and a track record of following through on both relationships and tasks.
  • Genuine affinity for the mission and an understanding of the cultural and political landscape in which Galvanize operates.
  • Ability to travel as needed for cultivation events, regional salons, and donor meetings throughout the year.

Valued and Non-Essential Characteristics

  • Deep familiarity with the compliance structure of a multi-entity organization — or a demonstrated eagerness to learn it quickly.

Compensation & Benefits

The starting salary range for this position is $88,000-95,000. Placement within this band will be determined based on years of prior experience and relevant skills. Galvanize USA also offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance for employees (and their families). Employees are able to enroll in the 401k retirement plan and are eligible for a 3% automatic contribution and up to a 3% employer match on 401k contributions. Employees are also eligible for pre-tax transportation benefits. Employees will receive 120 hours of vacation time, 80 hours of health leave, up to 2 days of casual leave, and 20 hours of volunteer leave annually. Employees will also receive 13 paid holidays throughout the calendar year. Employees are eligible for 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave after 90 days of employment.

How to Apply

Submit a resume and respond to custom application questions. Applications will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applications received by August 19 will be given preference.

Sometimes our emails end up in spam—please keep an eye on your spam folder just in case.

About Galvanize USA

Galvanize USA is a nonpartisan civic empowerment program for women who want to help build an America that works for everyone - white, Black, and brown. Women who participate in Galvanize USA programming gain confidence, knowledge, and skills to more fully and authentically engage in civic life. We believe in unlocking the power of every woman to advance progress for all.

The person holding this position will also work part-time for a coordinated project, Galvanize Action, in the Sixteen Thirty Fund, a 501(c)(4) organization, under a resource sharing agreement between the Hopewell Fund and Sixteen Thirty Fund. The responsibilities under that position will be overseen by Sixteen Thirty Fund. Galvanize Action identifies, engages, and moves moderate women in rural, small town, and suburban America to reliably support progress. To learn more visit galvanizeaction.org.

Hiring Statement

Galvanize USA is a project of Hopewell Fund, a 501(c)(3) public charity that incubates new and innovative public-interest projects and grant-making programs. Hopewell Fund is committed to attracting, developing and retaining exceptional people, and to creating a work environment that is dynamic, rewarding and enables each of us to realize our potential. Hopewell Fund’s work environment is safe and open to all employees and partners, respecting the full spectrum of race, color, religious creed, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, political affiliation, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, and all other classifications protected by law in the locality and/or state in which you are working.

E-Verify

Hopewell participates in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with employees’ Form I-9 information to confirm authorization to work in the United States. Job candidates and employees authorized to work may not be discriminated against on the basis of national origin or citizenship status.

About AlphaSense:

Come join us!

Location: NYC, Remote based in Eastern or Central time zones

About the Team:

The extraordinary AlphaSense Sales team is split into two parts: Financial Services and Corporates. The Financial Services Sales Team focuses on sales to hedge funds, asset management, investment banking, and private equity. The Corporate Sales team is verticalized with a focus on the Fortune 1000 in the following sectors: Life Sciences, Technology, Media, and Telecom, Energy and Industrials, Consulting, and Consumer Packaged Goods. Both the Financial Services and Corporate sales teams have Enterprise and Mid-Market sales professionals, and there is an additional corporate team of sales professionals focused exclusively on Investor Relations.

We are looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial, driven and accomplished new business sales professional to join our growing Corporate Sales team. With a track record of sales success, you’ll focus on selling to top Fortune 1000 companies, specifically the largest and most matrixed organizations. This role offers a high level of ownership within your book of business, driving the overall account strategy in partnership with SDR’s and sales leadership. This is an opportunity to join a high growth company and sell an award winning product that is experiencing rapid adoption across all industry verticals. The person in this role will make a major contribution in the company’s growth and future success.

Who You Are:

  • An experienced seller! You have previous experience owning a book of new business, ideally selling into enterprise clients. You have a strong track record of success in a SaaS or non-SaaS sales environment and can clearly communicate a drive to understand our customers and sales cycle.
  • You understand Sales is both art and science, and clearly can articulate your version of the “science of sales”.

  • Intellectually Curious: You know the right questions to ask and how to uncover business challenges at all levels of an organization.
  • Coachable: You will have the opportunity to advance your career through robust training and development programs at AlphaSense. An openness to feedback and desire for constant improvement is key to success here.
  • Tenacious: You thrive in environments where you can be creative to get things done!

What You’ll Do:

  • Take responsibility for the end-end sales processes in your territory, targeting folks in Corporate Strategy, Competitive Intelligence, Business Development, Investor Relations, and M&A.
  • Research opportunities, prospect, initiate discussions, build relationships, conduct demos, manage product trials, and most importantly: close deals! This is an end-to-end new business sales role and no task is too small or too large.
  • Partner with our SDR team to create prospecting plans and drive pipeline.
  • Forecast accurately and develop the necessary pipeline to meet/exceed quota.
  • Work closely with our Product Specialist team during trials to ensure client engagement and ultimate purchase.
  • Work closely with Account Management to ensure customer health throughout the contract term, as well as closing down sourced upsell and cross-sell opportunities.
  • Gather and distribute product feedback from clients and prospects to the sales and product teams to help us continually enhance our product offerings.

For base compensation, we set standard ranges for all roles based on function and level benchmarked against similar stage growth companies and internal comparables. In order to be compliant with local legislation, as well as to provide greater transparency to candidates, we share salary ranges on all job postings regardless of desired hiring location. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience/expertise and may vary from the amounts listed below.

We offer a competitive benefits program, a generous commission plan with uncapped earning potential as well as equity.

Base Compensation Range
$105,000—$140,000 USD

AlphaSense is an equal-opportunity employer. We are committed to a work environment that supports, inspires, and respects all individuals. All employees share in the responsibility for fulfilling AlphaSense’s commitment to equal employment opportunity. AlphaSense does not discriminate against any employee or applicant on the basis of race, color, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, military or veteran status, disability, or any other non-merit factor. This policy applies to every aspect of employment at AlphaSense, including recruitment, hiring, training, advancement, and termination.

In addition, it is the policy of AlphaSense to provide reasonable accommodation to qualified employees who have protected disabilities to the extent required by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances where a particular employee works.

Recruiting Scams and Fraud

We at AlphaSense have been made aware of fraudulent job postings and individuals impersonating AlphaSense recruiters. These scams may involve fake job offers, requests for sensitive personal information, or demands for payment. Please note:

Who We Are

At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

Our Values

If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.

You are self-driven and like to work with others to remove roadblocks. You are curious and love to explore and learn new technologies. Instead of writing bespoke software for every workflow, we are developing an agent platform that can read operational knowledge, reason about it in context, and execute tasks end-to-end. This approach allows us to scale complexity through knowledge and reasoning, rather than simply through code.

This is an opportunity to join a foundational team, which currently consists of fewer than five engineers. The work spans critical areas including LLM-powered agent design, robust backend service architecture, tool and integration development, and sophisticated knowledge infrastructure.

  • You are pragmatic and balance quality with speed. You understand when to optimize for long-term durability and when to iterate quickly. You prioritize pragmatism over being overly precious about code, but never compromise on quality in a way that creates future issues.
  • You are product-minded. You look beyond the immediate task, seeking to understand the "why" behind the build and questioning whether it's the right product solution. You are comfortable contributing product thinking alongside engineering work.
  • You demonstrate a strong ownership mindset. You are proactive, identify gaps, and drive initiatives to completion without waiting for explicit instructions. When encountering issues or ambiguity, you address them directly.
  • You possess strong backend engineering fundamentals. You can confidently design, build, and operate production systems.
  • You are curious and eager to develop expertise in AI and LLMs. While deep research is not required, you are motivated to build practical, real-world products using these tools, specifically focusing on agent systems.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of backend engineering experience building and operating production systems
  • Hands-on experience with LLMs and AI agents (orchestration, RAG, tool/function calling, or similar)
  • Strong API design and system integration skills
  • Product-minded: questions requirements and contributes to product decisions, not just execution
  • Proven ownership of complex projects in ambiguous, early-stage environments

Technologies Used

  • Golang, Ruby on Rails, Javascript, Java, C#, Python, VueJS, MySQL, Kafka, AWS, Git, Memcache, Redis, ElasticSearch, Docker, Terraform, Kubernetes, CircleCI, DataDog

The Role: If the idea of dialing for dollars makes you want to close the tab, keep reading. This role isn't that. You've been selling your expertise all along but you just never called it sales. At Seer, you'll take that instinct and apply it to one of the most intellectually honest growth practices in the industry: building (inbound) relationships with major brands, figuring out which ones we can actually help, and building the strategy to prove it.

Role Highlights
